What you need to capture

What the app shows you.

Sign in with your email, practise on one small room, then check the saved route before you send anything.

Screens from the current build in the iOS Simulator; on a real iPhone the camera fills the capture screen. The app is in invite-only testing through TestFlight.

One space, five steps.

  1. Choose the space and scope.

    Decide the rooms and the private areas to exclude. Each capture is one walkthrough, with one link and one QR code. The app shows how many rooms fit in one capture; a home with more rooms takes more captures, and each is its own walkthrough with its own link. Keep street addresses and access instructions out of anything you share.

  2. Prepare and capture.

    Clear personal documents and screens, keep people and pets out of the route, and keep lighting steady. Walk the space with the phone upright and follow the capture guidance. Review the saved photographs and route checks before leaving; those checks do not prove capture quality. After you send it, an automatic quality check assesses capture quality.

  3. Automatic processing and quality check.

    Send from the app: it uploads in the background and is usually ready in 1–2 hours. Veylet reconstructs it automatically; no person checks it, and recording on the phone does not create a finished tour by itself. An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work, such as one with no usable photos or depth, and asks for a recapture of the rooms it names; anything else it finds is flagged as worth a look for you to check before you approve. The 1–2 hours count from when the upload finishes, and you review it before anyone else sees it. Your original stays on the iPhone. A capture that cannot be used is never counted.

  4. Review before sharing.

    Open it on your phone and walk every room: turns, doorways, floor and ceiling edges, and anything private. Look at each area flagged as worth a look. If rooms need fixing, recapture them: the recapture replaces the walkthrough on the same link and uses no walkthrough. Each accepted walkthrough counts toward the 6 included in your free months, or toward your plan’s allowance after them. You need permission to capture the space and to publish it.

  5. Share on your terms.

    Tick “I have the right to share this walkthrough.” and press Approve and share: one press puts its link, QR code and embed live. Copy them from the app or your desk. Viewers need no account or capture app. Anyone who receives the link can forward it.

    Add a tour to your agency website

Your first session: one practice capture.

For every new account.

The app unlocks real captures once your practice room passes. Nobody has to approve you: the practice room is checked in the app.

  1. Check the device and install the app.Capture needs an iPhone 12 Pro or a later Pro model, or an iPad Pro with LiDAR; the phone’s Settings › General › About shows its model. When your account is admitted, the invitation email has the install link. Sign in with the email you joined with.
  2. Record one small practice room.Choose a room you may capture, clear private items and follow the in-app movement prompts. Branding, team invitations and website setup can wait.
  3. Inspect what you saved.Open the saved photographs and check coverage before leaving. A saved capture is your first checkpoint; it is not a finished walkthrough. Keep the original if you want another attempt.
  4. Send it from the app.Tap Send to Veylet. Send from the app: it uploads in the background and is usually ready in 1–2 hours. Veylet processes the capture automatically and an automatic quality check assesses the result. Your original stays on the iPhone.

Stuck at sign-in or sending? Keep your capture and tell Veylet support which step stopped, the device model and app build. Do not include passwords, access codes or private images in an email. New accounts are admitted in weekly groups. Sign in with the email you joined with.

Keep the handover simple.

Already admitted?

Use the email you joined with on both the website and capture app. Sign in, then save a space.

When the listing changes.

Revoke the handoff and remove its embed when the tour should stop being available. Revocation blocks new access; it cannot erase copies already downloaded. Your walkthroughs stay live while your plan runs; to delete one, ask Veylet support.

Before you start.

What if the first result is not usable?

A capture that cannot be used is never counted: the automatic quality check names the rooms to recapture, and a recapture of them uses no walkthrough and keeps the same link. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free: the redo corrects it on the same link and uses no walkthrough, though a new capture visit is not included. Keep the original on your iPhone and tell Veylet support which area is wrong. Nothing is shared until you approve it.

Can every visitor open a tour?

Visitors use a current browser with graphics support on a phone, tablet or computer. Performance depends on the tour, device and connection. Share a direct link as a fallback for website builders that block embedded content. Portal compatibility must be checked with that portal.

Can an agency use it free?

Eligible App Store subscribers, or accounts with an agreed invoiced start, receive 3 free months with 6 accepted walkthroughs in total. They begin when the plan is activated with a payment method on file, and there is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace. The first charge is on the day they end; cancel before then and nothing is charged. App Store subscriptions renew at the price of the plan you chose, monthly or annual, unless cancelled through Apple. Invoiced service continues only under explicitly agreed and settled terms; it does not auto-renew. On the monthly Veylet plan each paid month includes 2 accepted walkthroughs, and unused ones roll over, up to 4 banked; the annual plan has 24 to use any time in the plan year, and 4 bonus walkthroughs and 4 Super fast renders if you choose it before your free months end. For a busier month the account owner can add a pack of 3 or 10 walkthroughs, valid 12 months, including during the free months. Check the renewal date on your account; you can cancel any time. Every walkthrough you released stays live while your plan runs; when it ends, its links keep working for 14 days, then go offline until you restart it. While capture quality is still being proven we onboard accounts in cohorts, so ask about availability before promising a client a date.

Is a walkthrough a measured survey?

No. It provides visual context for a space. It is not a measured floor plan, building survey or guarantee of condition. Keep listing photography and required property information available alongside it.
